prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In an outdoor work site with a row of metal electrical cabinets and dirt ground, the depth map places the camera wearer's extended right hand and tool (frames 1-2) and the resting hard hats and walkie-talkie on the foreground cabinet (frames 1-3) brightest at about 0.3 to 0.7 metres away, within direct arm's reach. A co-worker in a hard hat and reflective vest stands roughly 0.8 to 1.2 metres to the left in frames 1-2 facing right toward the cabinets, remains about 1.2 metres in front as the wearer turns left in frame 3 while he faces and looks slightly downward rather than at the wearer, and appears very bright at 0.5 to 0.8 metres on the right in frames 4-5 as the camera pitches down and he crouches within reach of the wearer. Behind the foreground cabinet and co-worker (about 0.5 to 1.5 metres separated from them), additional cabinets sit at roughly 1.5 to 3.5 metres in frames 1-3, while in frames 4-5 the downward view shows an open metal toolbox on the ground about 1.5 to 2 metres ahead to the left of the co-worker and ~1 metre from the cabinets, with cables trailing to 3-5 metres and distant slopes beyond. The depth map makes the stepped distance hierarchy across the receding row of grey cabinets and the continuous ground slope much clearer than in the uniform-toned RGB images, while also showing how the co-worker's lower legs and the cabinets are partly cropped or occluded at frame edges. However, the map is unreliable on the distant hillside and sky in frames 1-3 where both collapse to pure black, and it blurs fine thin structures like the walkie-talkie antenna, ground cables, and tool edges into adjacent surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground human figures against the unlabelled background of metal cabinets, hard hats, cables, and dirt ground across the five frames. In frames 1 and 2, it segments the co-worker partly cropped on the far left (at ~0.8-1.2 metres, facing right with his extended left hand within reach of the foreground cabinet) and separately segments the camera wearer's own right arm and hand reaching from the right edge at ~0.4-0.6 metres to place a yellow-and-blue tool onto the cabinet top. In frame 3, as the camera turns left, only the co-worker is segmented as a single central silhouette about 1.2 metres in front, facing forward and slightly down with his lower body cropped at the bottom edge. In frames 4 and 5, as the camera looks down toward the ground, the co-worker crouching on the right (at ~0.5-0.8 metres, facing left/downward toward his hands and within arm's reach of the wearer) is split into multiple overlapping 'person' masks, while the open metal toolbox resting on the dirt about 1.5-2 metres ahead and ~1 metre to the co-worker's left issegmented as a separate polygon. This map clearly distinguishes the camera wearer's own reaching limb from the co-worker and background machinery in frames 1-2, but it is highly unreliable where it misclassifies the ground toolbox as a 'boat' in frames 4-5, fragments the crouching co-worker's torso and legs into separate overlapping 'person' instances with holes, and completely misses the cabinets, hard hats, and hand tools.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints on a black background, capturing only subsets of the people present across the five frames as the camera pans left and tilts down. In frame 1, only a magenta hand skeleton is detected for the camera wearer's right hand reaching at ~0.4 metres on the right to hold a tool above the cabinet, while the co-worker standing ~1 metre away on the far left (facing right with his head and torso partly cropped) is completely missed by both body and hand detectors in frames 1 and 2, as is the wearer's hand in frame 2. In frame 3, a yellow upper-body and hip skeleton with facial keypoints appears for the co-worker standing ~1.2 metres in front, showing his shoulders square to the camera, his head angled slightly down rather than looking directly at the wearer, his arms hanging down near his waist within reach of his own torso, and his legs occluded below the frame edge. In frame 4, a sideways yellow skeleton on the right at ~0.6-0.8 metres captures the co-worker's torso and bent legs as he crouches facing left toward the ground, whereas frame 5 is completely blank despite his right arm, torso, and legs remaining visible and within arm's reach in the lower-right corner. The pose map explicitly reveals the co-worker's shoulder orientation, head pitch, and crouching limb articulation in frames 3-4 that are partially obscured by loose clothing and shadows in the RGB view, but it is unreliable whenever bodies or hands are heavily truncated at frame boundaries (frames 1, 2, and 5) and misses the co-worker's hands in all frames.
